answer: A glacier keeps its own ledger: every layer is laid down once, in order, and cannot be copied onto another mountain. Bind each identity to a hardware enclave key burned into one chip, and the fable of a thousand agents on one machine dies there, because an enclave signature cannot be cloned in software. Each fake must buy real silicon and pass its own attestation, and the pearl of the proof is that the key never leaves the chip. A farm cannot share one enclave across identities, parallelize a single attestation, or bulk-buy its way around physics: one device, one identity, one cost.
